bim.room.title: Use a room from the model
bim.room.note: Lists the rooms the walls of the open model enclose, the ones that touch the walls you have selected first. The room becomes the job's room and its doors and windows become the job's openings; the cabinets are then placed on that level.
bim.nolevel: The model has no level to put the cabinets on.
bim.place.title: Cabinets in the model
bim.place.note: Makes every cabinet, filler and end panel a piece of furniture in the model (IfcFurniture; IfcFurnishingElement in IFC2X3) and every countertop piece a building element proxy, standing on the level the room came from, each with a solid of one prism per panel and a CabinetCraft property set (number, template, run, size, elevation, material, job). One undo step. Placing again replaces this job's elements.
bim.place.label: place cabinets
bim.place.assumed: No room was taken from the model, so they stand on the first level at its origin.
bim.place.empty: This job has no cabinets yet.
bim.remove.label: remove cabinets
bim.removed: {n} elements taken out of the model.
bim.none: None of this job's elements are in the model.
bim.count: {n} elements of this job are in the model.
bim.count.unknown: Open a model to place the cabinets.
bim.model.title: Schedule from the model
bim.model.note: Reads the schedule back from the elements in the model, so it shows what is really there. The cut list is the job's (Export above); each element carries its cabinet number so the two can be matched.
bim.model.nosite: Take a room from the model first (Room tab) so the job knows its level.
bim.check: Check the model against the job
bim.check.ok: The model has all {n} elements of the job and nothing else.
bim.check.diff: The model and the job differ: {missing} missing, {extra} extra ({list}). Place again to bring the model up to date.
bim.draft.title: Plan on the level's plan view
bim.draft.note: Draws the job's plan (room outline, cabinets, countertops, doors, windows) as drafting lines in the plan view of the level, so it shows in the plan views and on sheets. One undo step; drawing again replaces it. Elevations and sections of the cabinets are BimCraft's own, cut from the elements; the job's own set can be saved above as a printable sheet set.
bim.draft.do: Draw the plan on the level
bim.draft.label: plan drawing
